stateData.name: Vermont
stateData.summary: Fully exempt below the threshold; a partial exemption phases out at higher incomes rather than disappearing all at once.
stateData.note: Some sources cite $55K/$70K or $65K/$85K instead — variance likely reflects different tax years. Confirm current figure before publishing.

otherStates.name: Colorado
otherStates.summary: Fully exempt at age 65+. Ages 55-64 fully exempt if AGI is at or below the threshold; above it, only a partial deduction applies. Under 55, no special SS exemption.
otherStates.note: SB25-136 (effective Jan 1, 2026) also removed caps on the separate pension/annuity subtraction — mention this as a 2026-specific update.

otherStates.name: Connecticut
otherStates.summary: Fully exempt if AGI is at or below the threshold. Above it, no more than 25% of federally taxable benefits become subject to Connecticut tax.

otherStates.name: Minnesota
otherStates.summary: Fully exempt below the threshold; the exemption phases out gradually (10% reduction per $4,000 of income above the threshold) rather than disappearing all at once.
otherStates.note: 2025 figures cited across sources; confirm 2026 inflation-adjusted numbers before publishing.

seo.title: Is Social Security Taxed in Vermont? (2026 Rules)
seo.description: Is Social Security taxed in Vermont in 2026? Yes, but benefits are fully exempt below $50k single ($65k joint), with partial phaseouts. See VT rules.
